meta.titre: Family and Community Life: homes, roles and living together
meta.sous_theme: Types of family and parent, roles in the home, broken homes and community values

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Citizenship Education past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: In many Cameroonian neighbourhoods people help each other at weddings and funerals, and contribute to savings groups such as njangi. The first place where a child learns respect, sharing and responsibility is the family, and the second is the community. The GCE tests the names of the types of parents and homes, the duties of family members and the values of community life. Knowing the vocabulary exactly is half of the marks.

items: A family is a group of people related by blood, marriage or adoption.
Parents are the father and the mother, or guardians, who bring up a child.
A community is a group of people who live in the same area and share common interests.

sections.titre: The family, the home and the community
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Members and kinds of parent
The home has three main components: the **parents or guardians**, the **children** and **other relatives** such as grandparents, uncles and aunts. Kinds of parent:
- **Biological parents** gave birth to the child.
- **Adoptive parents** legally take a child as their own and bring the child up for life.
- **Foster parents** look after a child for a period without becoming the child's legal parents.
- **A guardian** is a person who looks after a child whose parents cannot.
- **A step-parent** is the husband or wife of one of the child's parents.

### Types of family
| Type | Members |
|---|---|
| Nuclear | Parents and their children |
| Extended | Parents, children and other relatives living together |
| Single-parent | One parent and the children |
| Polygamous | One man with more than one wife and their children |

### Happy and broken homes
In a **happy home** members show love, respect and understanding, and they talk to each other. A **broken home** is one marked by constant conflict, separation or divorce.

### Roles in the home
| Parents | Children |
|---|---|
| Provide food, shelter, clothing and health care | Obey and respect their parents |
| Send children to school | Study hard |
| Give love and discipline | Help with household tasks |
| Teach good moral values | Care for parents when they grow old |

### Community life
A good community is built on **solidarity, mutual help, respect for elders and traditional rulers, tolerance, honesty and cleanliness**. Citizens take part in community development work and help neighbours in need. Leaders include chiefs, fons and lamidos, religious leaders and councillors. Conflicts are best settled by dialogue and by mediation of elders or authorities.

### Broken homes
Causes include poverty, lack of communication, unfaithfulness and drug or alcohol abuse. Effects on children are poor school results, stress and a risk of delinquency. Solutions are dialogue, counselling and mediation.

variantes.nom: Questions on names of parents, homes and families
variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question describes a person or a home and asks for its name
variantes.contenu_markdown: Read the key idea in the description: legal and permanent means adoptive, temporary means foster, conflict and separation mean broken home, parents and their children only means nuclear.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks for duties of parents or children
variantes.contenu_markdown: Separate the two lists and give the duty with its result: parents provide food and shelter so that children grow healthy, children respect and obey their parents so that the home is peaceful.

variantes.nom: Questions on conflicts and broken homes
variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks about causes, effects or solutions
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give three clear groups: causes (poverty, poor communication, unfaithfulness, alcohol), effects (poor school performance, stress, delinquency, insecurity) and solutions (dialogue, counselling, mediation by elders or religious leaders).

sections.enonce_markdown: Explain three causes and two effects of broken homes. (10 marks)

etapes.action: Read the command word and count what is asked.
etapes.justification: Explain asks for reasons. You must give three causes and two effects, no more.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Define a broken home, then give 3 causes and 2 effects.

etapes.action: Define the term in one sentence.
etapes.justification: A definition shows that you understand the term and it opens the answer.
etapes.resultat_markdown: A broken home is one in which conflict, separation or divorce prevents the members from living in harmony.

etapes.action: Write each cause with its explanation.
etapes.justification: A cause with a reason earns more marks than a list.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Poverty: when parents cannot meet basic needs, quarrels develop. Poor communication: problems are not discussed, so misunderstanding grows. Unfaithfulness: it destroys trust between the husband and wife.

etapes.action: Write each effect with its explanation.
etapes.justification: Effects must concern the members of the family, particularly the children.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Poor performance at school: the child is stressed and cannot concentrate. Delinquency: without guidance the child may follow bad companions.

sections.conclusion_markdown: Model answer: A broken home is a home in which conflict, separation or divorce prevents members from living in harmony. One cause is poverty: when parents cannot provide basic needs, quarrels develop. Another cause is poor communication: problems are not discussed, so misunderstanding grows. A third cause is unfaithfulness, which destroys trust between husband and wife. Broken homes affect children. They may perform poorly at school because they are stressed and cannot concentrate. They may also drift into delinquency because they lack guidance and follow bad companions.

items.erreur_markdown: "Foster parents and adoptive parents are the same."
items.pourquoi_faux: Adoptive parents take a child as their own for life. Foster parents look after a child only for a period of time.
items.correction_markdown: Adoptive: legal and permanent. Foster: temporary care.

items.erreur_markdown: "A home with only one parent is always a broken home."
items.pourquoi_faux: A single-parent home can be happy and stable. A broken home is described by conflict, separation or divorce.
items.correction_markdown: Call it a single-parent family, and use broken home only for a home marked by conflict or separation.

items.erreur_markdown: "The mother alone is responsible for bringing up the children."
items.pourquoi_faux: Both parents share the duty to feed, educate and guide the children.
items.correction_markdown: Write that parents, not only the mother, are responsible, and give the shared duties.

items.erreur_markdown: "Community life means helping only your relatives."
items.pourquoi_faux: Community life includes neighbours and other members of the community, whether or not they are related.
items.correction_markdown: Say that community life means solidarity and mutual help among all members.

items.erreur_markdown: "Children have rights but no duties in the home."
items.pourquoi_faux: Children also have duties, such as obedience, respect, helping with household tasks and studying.
items.correction_markdown: Give both the rights and the duties of the child.

items.enonce_markdown: (a) What is a nuclear family? (b) Name two other types of family.
items.solution_markdown: (a) A nuclear family consists of parents and their children only. (b) Any two: extended family, single-parent family, polygamous family. Award marks for the definition and for each type.

items.enonce_markdown: A husband and wife quarrel almost every day over money and neither listens to the other. Explain three ways in which the problem can be solved.
items.solution_markdown: Any three, each with a reason: talk calmly together, so that each person understands the other; draw up a simple budget together, so that spending follows shared priorities; ask elders, religious leaders or a counsellor to mediate, so that a neutral person helps them to find a solution; look for ways to increase the family income, so that financial pressure falls; set aside time to listen and to forgive, so that trust is rebuilt. Award a mark for each way and a mark for its reason.

items.enonce_markdown: Discuss four ways in which members of a community can live peacefully together and contribute to its development.
items.solution_markdown: Any four with explanation: respect for elders and traditional leaders, so that order is kept; tolerance of differences in religion and origin, so that conflicts are avoided; taking part in community work such as cleaning the quarter, so that the environment is healthy; mutual help in times of need such as sickness, weddings and funerals, so that nobody is left alone; settling quarrels by dialogue and mediation rather than violence; honesty and respect for public property. Conclusion: a peaceful community is built by the daily attitudes of its members. Award marks for each point with reason and for a conclusion.

items_markdown: The home consists of parents or guardians, children and other relatives. Learn the names: biological, adoptive, foster, step-parent and guardian.
Types of family: nuclear, extended, single-parent and polygamous.
A happy home is marked by love, respect and communication. A broken home is marked by conflict, separation or divorce.
Parents provide for, educate and guide the children. Children obey, respect, study and help at home.
Community life relies on solidarity, mutual help, respect for elders, tolerance and peaceful settlement of conflicts.
